- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged mean.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast gradually, not abruptly.
- Mean reversion bias: if model consistently forecasts above 85% of recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth forecast with 5-day moving average of true values if sentiment is volatile.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- Avoid forecasting above 85% of 30-day true mean unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.80) and recent price is accelerating.
